previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe diastolic heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, atrial fibrillation, and recent MRSA pneumonia completed a course of vancomycin and presented for PICC line removal. He was found to be confused and fatigued, with lab results showing acute kidney injury, elevated BUN and creatinine, and worsening anemia. His symptoms were attributed to uremia from pre-renal azotemia due to aggressive diuresis. Diuretics were held for 36 hours, after which his kidney function improved, mental status returned to baseline, and anemia stabilized without intervention. He was discharged on adjusted medications, including reduced metoprolol and a modified torsemide regimen, with instructions to monitor weight and follow up with neurology for persistent myoclonic jerks.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast head CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images of the brain were obtained without

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or large
territorial infarction.  Mild prominence of ventricles and sulci are
consistent with age-related cortical volume loss.  The basal cisterns are
patent and there is preservation of gray-white matter differentiation.  Faint
periventricular and subcortical hypodensities are likely sequelae of chronic
small vessel ischemic disease.

No fracture is seen.  No soft tissue hematoma or extra-axial fluid collection.
There is mild mucosal thickening of the ethmoid and sphenoid sinuses
bilaterally with under-pneumatization and partial opacification of bilateral
mastoid air cells. Additional visualized paranasal sinuses and middle ear
cavities are clear.  The globes are unremarkable. Locules of gas within the
infratemporal fossa bilaterally and cavernous sinuses likely relate to
intravenous manipulation.

IMPRESSION:  Chronic changes as described above, otherwise negative head CT.

The stomach, duodenum and small bowel are within normal limits, without
